A new Scrolling layout you can move with your fingers, and a workspace bar you can shape to your liking.
### New - Scrolling layout (Pro): windows sit side by side as columns on a strip wider than the display, always starting at a window's left edge, with the next one peeking in on the right. Scrolling moves the whole strip in one smooth motion that follows quick key presses without waiting. Hyper ← / → and clicking a window scroll it into view; Hyper ⇧ ← / → moves a column along it, and you can drag a window between columns or onto another display's strip. New windows open next to the focused one. Resize a window to change its column's width, or use Column wider / narrower (⅓, ½, ⅔, full) from search or a shortcut you assign. - Hold Hyper and scroll over the Scrolling layout to move the strip with your fingers; let go and it glides on and settles at a window's edge. A mouse wheel moves one window per notch. Optionally, a three-finger swipe does the same without a key. Trackpad, mouse and swipe speeds are in Settings → Windows → Scrolling layout. - Hyper ⇧ + arrow keys now send the focused window to the next display in that direction once there is no other window that way in its layout. It takes the nearest empty slot of a layout there, or floats at the same spot on a display without one.
### Improved - Switching to Scrolling keeps your windows' sizes: a window comes in as wide as it was in the previous layout, and widths and column order you set in Scrolling come back when you return to it from another layout. Choosing Scrolling again while it's active still sets every column to half. - The workspace bar lists a Scrolling display's windows in the order of its columns, and dragging a window along the bar moves its column on the strip. - The workspace bar can center its windows (Alignment in the bar's right-click menu, or Settings → Windows → Workspaces). - The workspace bar's options open with a right-click anywhere on the bar, replacing the ⋯ button. The workspace numbers, the layout menu and the clock can each be hidden (right-click → Show, or Settings). - Liquid Glass in the workspace bar is now see-through glass that bends the desktop at its edges; on macOS 27 it looked the same as frosted Glass. - Layouts feel quicker: switching layouts several times in a row goes straight to the last one, windows of all apps start sliding together, and Hyper arrow presses made in quick succession are no longer dropped.
### Fixes - Chrome and Firefox windows could be seen flying to the screen corner when another window took their place in a layout.

Design your own layouts, keep windows clear of third-party docks, and find out when another app is using Wimi's shortcuts too.
### New - Custom layouts (Pro): make your own layout from up to four columns of one to three stacked windows, and drag its dividers to set the sizes. Start from the New Layout card in Layouts, right-click a layout to edit or copy it, or click Save as Layout to keep the shape you've dragged your windows into. Custom layouts work in search, the workspace bar menu and Next / Previous layout.
### Improved - Screen margins: in Settings → Windows, set how much space layouts leave free at the top, bottom, left and right of each display, so windows stay clear of third-party docks such as DockDoor or other bars that cover them. - When another app, such as Raycast or Rectangle, reacts to one of Wimi's shortcuts and moves your windows too, Wimi now tells you once and names the window managers that are running, so you can remove the duplicate shortcut.
### Fixes - A window too big for its slot no longer trades places with its neighbor when you focus it with Hyper + arrow keys. - Temporary license-server errors, rate limits and firewall responses no longer remove an activated license. Failed deactivation keeps the license and activation ID so you can retry. - Turning on Hyper no longer erases other key remappings, such as `hidutil` remaps or macOS's per-keyboard modifier key settings. Turning it off or quitting restores the previous Caps Lock mapping. - Entering a license key for a different product no longer uses up one of that key's activations. - Unplugging an external keyboard no longer releases Hyper or modifiers you're holding on another keyboard.

Layouts that leave your windows usable: they get their size back when they leave a layout, and apps that can't shrink to fit no longer push their neighbors off screen.
### New - Reset a layout's window sizes, for example to get 2/3 – 1/3 back after dragging it to halves: choose the active layout again (click it, pick it from the workspace bar or press its shortcut), press Hyper 0 (⌃⌥⌘0), or search "Reset layout sizes". Change the key in Settings → Shortcuts. - New setting in Settings → Windows, "Put windows back when quitting Wimi": tiled windows return to where they were before Wimi arranged them. - What's New… in the menu bar menu opens the changelog at getwimi.app/changelog, in case you closed the update notes too quickly.
### Improved - Apps that can't get as small as their slot (Notion, Xcode) now overlap the window next to them instead of squeezing it or pushing it off screen, so every window stays usable. The window you're using stays on top; click the other to bring it forward. A warning sign in the workspace bar, the window switcher and the Layouts view says which app needs more room. - Turning a layout off puts every window back where it was before Wimi tiled it, not just the hidden ones. - With "Moving a window yourself: Takes it out of the layout", dragging a window out of its slot gives it back its original size.

Fixes for setups with several displays, and faster workspace switches.
### Improved - Switching workspaces starts about twice as fast, and windows of apps with windows in both workspaces (Safari, Finder) no longer pause mid-slide. - The first time Wimi hides a window, it offers once to open Desktop & Dock settings if "Group windows by application" is off, which keeps Mission Control readable.
### Fixes - Hidden windows no longer stay visible or move to another workspace when a display's bottom corners are blocked by its neighbors, as can happen with three monitors or a laptop above a wider display. - Dragging a tiled window to a display without a layout gives it back the size it had before the layout. - Dragging a staged window to a smaller display no longer snaps it back or shrinks your saved staged size. - Windows that Wimi places freely (dragged to a display without a layout, or popped out) no longer cover the workspace bar. - Windows waiting behind a layout in another workspace stay in that workspace when a display disconnects. - Switching workspaces tries again if a busy app missed the move, so its window doesn't stay hidden.

Wimi 1.0: free to use, with Wimi Pro for the power features. Everyone gets 30 days of Pro to try it, and for six weeks Pro is half price.
### Free and Pro Wimi stays free: the drawer, the window switcher with live previews and ⌥Tab, search, the app launcher, emoji, Keep Awake, the Hyper key, and the Fullscreen, Staged and Halves layouts.
**Wimi Pro** adds: - **Advanced layouts:** thirds, quarters, 2/3–1/3, stacked and main+side. - **Staged window size:** size the staged window with a slider in the Layouts drawer or by dragging its edges. Each display and workspace keeps its own size. This replaces the Small/Medium/Large setting. - **Workspaces** and the **workspace bar**, including the workspace number in the menu bar. - **The always-visible strip.** - **Clipboard history.** - **Glass themes:** Glass, Liquid Glass, Sheet and Midnight.
Pro is **$19.99 once** (plus tax): no subscription, and your key works on two Macs. **Launch offer: $9.99 with the code LAUNCH50 until December 22.** Buy it from Settings → License, where you also enter your key.
**Updating from a beta?** Thank you for testing! Everything stays unlocked for 30 days from this update. After that, Wimi keeps working on the free plan, and your Pro settings (layouts, workspaces, the bar, your theme) wait for you until you buy. Nothing is deleted.
### New - **Settings → License:** see your trial, buy Pro and enter your key. The sparkle button above Settings in the drawer takes you there. - **Settings → Feedback:** email us from your mail app (or copy the address) or report a bug on GitHub. - With all workspaces shown, the window switcher can list windows most recently used first instead of grouped by workspace ("Group by workspace" in the drawer footer and Settings → Windows). The workspace bar keeps its grouping. - The welcome tour ends with a page about Wimi Pro and where your trial stands.
### Improved - The drawer can reopen on the tab you left it on: Settings → General → Open in → Last used tab. Scrolling over the drawer's tab bar switches tabs. - The drawer's see-through backgrounds (Transparency, Sheet, Glass, Liquid Glass) have a half-transparent wash behind the content, so text stays readable over a bright desktop. - Wimi sends one anonymous event when your trial starts, so we know how many people try it: the event and the Wimi version, nothing else. Turn it off on the welcome screen or in Settings → General → Privacy.
### Fixes - Steam's windows show up in the window switcher and join layouts. Steam draws them from a helper process with its own title bar, which Wimi used to skip. - ⌘Tab or a Dock click to Finder switches to the workspace holding its window, like every other app. Clicking the desktop still doesn't switch.
### Install Wimi 0.3.0 and later update themselves: use Check for Updates… in the menu bar, or wait for the daily check. Otherwise download `Wimi-1.0.0-9.dmg` below, open it and drag Wimi into Applications (replace the old version). Requires macOS 14 or later. Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.
